intro: San Francisco is the most expensive city we track. Listings advertise 10x10 units from about $142, while typical non-climate 10x10 street rates run about $266–$299/month. Once the move-in special ends and the first existing-customer increase lands, your six-month average is well above the number on the banner.
data_asof: Aug–Oct 2026 (StorageCafe, SpareFoot, Storage Stats); some sizes single-source estimates

units.notes: Locker / closet size. SpareFoot figure is from a small sample of booked units (Aug 2026). Climate-controlled ~$121–$186.

Most rented size. City average $299 (StorageCafe, Sep 2026, up 2.1% YoY); SF–Oakland metro averages $266 (Storage Stats), so East Bay facilities are often cheaper. A small SpareFoot sample averaged $464 and was excluded as an outlier. Climate-controlled ~$318.
Two-bedroom contents. Estimate: single source for the average (StorageCafe, Sep 2026). Climate-controlled ~$421.
Three-bedroom home or a car. Estimate: single source for the average (StorageCafe, Sep 2026); listed units are scarce. Climate-controlled ~$576.

local_tips: Supply is tight: StorageCafe counts only 27 facilities in the city, so promos are smaller and less common than in Texas.
Cheaper areas per StorageCafe include Ingleside Heights (~$197), the Inner Mission (~$207) and Dogpatch (~$227); Hunters Point is the most expensive (~$397). Oakland averages about $194 for a 10x10.
Rates tend to be lowest around January and highest in June (StorageCafe).
Ask about rate locks in writing — with few competitors nearby, existing-customer increases are harder to negotiate.
